turns.speaker: user
turns.text: How big can I print a photo from my phone before it looks bad?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Most modern phones are fine up to about A three for a wall, especially if you view it from a little distance.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Changing the subject, we've bought a house, but my son is halfway through the school year.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Tricky timing. Is the new house in a different school area?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Then you could move now and switch schools mid year, or move now and drive him to his old school until summer. Which would he prefer?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Okay, twelve seconds on the clock, then hit me with it again.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Which way for your son, switch now or finish the year?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: We'll drive him. He's got exams and his friends are there.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Sensible. It's only a few months, and he can visit the new school before September.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I want it huge, over the sofa.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Then it depends on the photo. Sharp, well lit shots in daylight hold up much better than dark ones or ones where you zoomed in.
